capitals.name: London
capitals.note: The page names no capital: 'The territory included the remains of two provincial Roman capitals, Colchester and London', and Bede records Bishop Mellitus arriving in London in 604. London is a placeholder for the kingdom's chief city until it 'had fallen to Mercia' in the mid-8th century (year bridged).

ledger.note: 527: Æscwine founds the kingdom of the East Saxons. Infobox 'Established: 527'; 'a date of 527 is given for the start of his reign, but there are some difficulties with the date'. It 'covered the territory later occupied by the counties of Essex, Middlesex, much of Hertfordshire' and held west Kent 'for a short while'. The counterpart is Cliopatria's Anglo-Saxon England, which contains the shape until 533 (bridged; the page names no earlier state).

region.text: the territory 'later occupied by the counties of Essex, Middlesex, much of Hertfordshire' with London and Colchester

ledger.note: c. 604: Æthelberht of Kent becomes Sæberht's overlord. He 'was in a position to exercise some authority in Essex shortly after 604'; Bede records Mellitus arriving in London in 604; the Æthelberht page calls him Sæberht's overlord and says it was he, not Sæberht, who 'built and endowed St. Pauls in London'. The vassal's record: the counterpart is the overlord.

region.text: the territory 'later occupied by the counties of Essex, Middlesex, much of Hertfordshire' with London and Colchester

ledger.note: 616: Sæberht dies and Kentish overlordship lapses. 'After the death of Sæberht in 616, Mellitus was driven out'; Æthelberht died on 24 February 616 (Æthelberht page). Neither page says the overlordship ended, so this is a bridge.

region.text: the territory 'later occupied by the counties of Essex, Middlesex, much of Hertfordshire' with London and Colchester

ledger.note: 664: the East Saxon kings rule under Wulfhere of Mercia. Swithhelm died in 664 and Sigehere and Sæbbi succeeded, 'rulers ... under Wulfhere, king of the Mercians' (Bede). The Essex page says the rebellion of Sigehere and Sæbbi 'was suppressed by Wulfhere of Mercia' with no year. Cliopatria ends its Essex row in 665. [Reviewer eu-11-b: the Essex infobox status line gives 'Independent kingdom (527–709) Client state of Mercia (709–825)'; 664 rests on Bede via the Wulfhere page and is kept.]

region.text: West Kent (Rochester and the Thames side); the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 689: East Saxon kings are active in west Kent. '689-690: East Saxon kings under Mercian overlordship were active in West Kent'; the Essex page: it held west Kent 'for a short while'. The Wihtred page names Swæfheard, son of Sebbi of Essex, as king in west Kent. [Reviewer eu-11-b: the Essex page puts it in the 8th century ('For a brief period in the 8th century, the Kingdom of Essex controlled west Kent'); 689 follows the Kent and Wihtred pages.]

ledger.note: 692: the East Saxon kingship in west Kent ends. Swæfheard 'is last mentioned in July 692' and 'by 694 Wihtred was the sole ruler of Kent'; the page does not say how it ended, so this is a bridge.

ledger.note: 825: Sigered cedes Essex to Ecgberht of Wessex. 'Sigered... in 825 ceded the kingdom to Ecgberht, King of Wessex'; infobox 'Full integration into the kingdom of Wessex: 825'; the Ellendun page: 'The West Saxons succeeded in conquering Sussex, Kent, and Essex'.

wars.name: Mercian suppression of the East Saxon rebellion
wars.outcome: The page: the rebellion of Sigehere and Sæbbi 'was suppressed by Wulfhere of Mercia'; the East Saxon kings were thereafter 'under Wulfhere'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The Essex page gives no year; 664 is the year of the plague and of Sigehere's apostasy on the Wulfhere page, which does not mention a rebellion.

wars.name: East Saxon rule in west Kent

zones.text: West Kent (Rochester and the Thames side); the page gives no boundary

wars.outcome: East Saxon kings under Mercian overlordship held west Kent for a short while; Wihtred was sole king of Kent by 694.

wars.name: West Saxon conquest of the south-east (Ellendun)
wars.outcome: Ecgberht beat Beornwulf at Ellendun in September 825; Sigered ceded Essex to Ecgberht.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on any page opened: the Thames and Stour and the Lea are not named as frontiers; the Hertfordshire edge ('much of Hertfordshire') and west Kent are the softest.

notes: Cliopatria's Essex row (534..665) is extended to 825 on the page's own end date: the kingdom lasted under Mercian overlordship (vassal from 664) until Sigered ceded it to Ecgberht. Its shape omits north-east Essex (Colchester), which Cliopatria gives to East Anglia (7 of the 8 missing cells overlap the East Anglia 534 shape); the Kingdom of East Anglia dossier removes the same cells. London and Middlesex are lost to Mercia at a bridged c. 750 (confidence 1). Mirror events needed in other dossiers: Mercia (vassal_start 664 and loss of London c. 750), Kent (the 604-616 overlordship over Essex, which this batch adds to kingdom-of-kent, and the 689-692 west Kent episode), Wessex (the 825 gain). The infobox gives no area. Not dated on a year: the 'intermittent control of Surrey', and the end of Kentish overlordship in 616. The Danelaw dossier takes Essex after the Treaty of Alfred and Guthrum (878-886).
